evidence.snippet: Courses taken at institutions outside the United States: College-level courses passed with a letter grade of C or higher completed outside the United States and recorded on official transcripts will be evaluated for transfer credit, provided that the institution where the courses were taken is accredited by the Ministry of Education in that country.

All academic courses successfully completed with a grade of C or higher at a fully accredited college or university are transferable; however, the University reserves the right to determine what constitutes an academic course.

Graduates of SUNY or CUNY colleges who earned an Associate in Arts or Associate in Science degree prior to matriculation at Stony Brook University receive transfer credit for all credits successfully completed as part of their associate degree requirements (with grades of C or higher).

evidence.snippet: Budget Increases Cornell Law School will grant budget increases on a limited case-by-case basis.

A budget increase may be granted for the following: Medical expenses not covered by insurance Computer replacement costs (one time and not to exceed $2,000) Required book costs These items may be considered on a case-by-case basis: Cost of living Travel Please note that cost of living increases may not be approved.

A budget increase will NOT be granted for: Car payments Consumer debt Furniture Summer living expenses Moving expenses Fall, Winter, and Spring break travel or trips Cell phones/internet service Sport and fitness club fees If you need a budget increase, contact the financial aid office at law.financialaid@cornell.edu.
Budget Increase Request form can be found in the forms section.
A: On a limited basis, the Financial Aid Review Committee may accept budget increases with proper documentation.
Submission deadlines are mid-November for fall requests and mid-April for fall/spring or spring only requests, please see the Budget Increase Request form in the forms section for specific dates.
